```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# The second NSF Engines competition, from letters of intent to awards (Cohort 2): the funnel, the sources,
# what was collected, and first findings. Data: py/00_competition_lists.py, py/00b_funnel_engines.py.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))
library(dplyr); library(readr); library(knitr); library(here); library(stringr)
props <- read_csv(here("data", "manual", "nsf_engines_c2_proposals.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
lois <- read_csv(here("data", "manual", "nsf_engines_c2_lois.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
chg <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "funnel_engines_change.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
reach <- function(s) sum(props$stage %in% s)
stages <- tibble(
  stage = c("Letters of intent", "Invited to full proposal", "Semifinalists", "Finalists", "NSF Engines"),
  when  = c("2024, data published July 2024", "after preliminary proposals (Aug 2024), Oct 2024",
            "after full proposals (Feb 2025), July 2025", "September 2025", "awards, 2026"),
  n     = c(nrow(lois), nrow(props), reach(c("semifinalist", "finalist", "engine")),
            reach(c("finalist", "engine")), reach("engine")))
```

The second NSF Regional Innovation Engines competition ran from 2024 to 2026. At each stage NSF published who
was still in the competition, so every team can be followed from its letter of intent to the award, or to the
stage where it stopped.

```{r funnel, results = "asis"}
# a funnel: one bar per stage; width by the square root of the number of teams, so the small stages differ
W <- 900; H <- 70; top <- 10
w <- W * sqrt(stages$n / max(stages$n))
bars <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(stages)), function(i) {
  x <- (W - w[i]) / 2; y <- top + (i - 1) * H
  sprintf(paste0('<rect x="%.0f" y="%d" width="%.0f" height="%d" fill="%s"/>',
                 '<text x="%d" y="%d" class="fn">%s</text>',
                 '<text x="%d" y="%d" class="fs">%s</text>',
                 '<text x="%.0f" y="%d" class="fk">%d</text>'),
          x, y, w[i], H - 12, if (i == nrow(stages)) "#2c3e50" else "#dfe7f2",
          W + 20, y + 24, stages$stage[i], W + 20, y + 46, stages$when[i],
          W / 2, y + 37, stages$n[i])
}, "")
cat(sprintf('<div style="overflow-x:auto"><svg viewBox="0 0 1380 %d" style="width:100%%; max-width:1000px; height:auto" role="img" aria-label="Funnel of the second NSF Engines competition">',
            top + nrow(stages) * H),
    '<style>.fn{font:700 21px Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;fill:#111}.fs{font:17px Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;fill:#555}',
    '.fk{font:700 24px Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;text-anchor:middle;fill:#111}</style>',
    sub('class="fk">(\\d+)</text>$', 'class="fk" style="fill:#fff">\\1</text>', bars[length(bars)]) |>
      (\(last) paste(c(bars[-length(bars)], last), collapse = ""))(),
    '</svg></div>', sep = "")
```

Before this competition, NSF gave 58 smaller planning grants (NSF Engines Development Awards, up to $1 million
for two years) in 2023-2024; many of the teams above held one. An NSF Engine award is up to $160 million for up
to 10 years.

## Sources

NSF published these lists to help teams find partners:

- [Letters of intent](https://new.nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/regional-innovation-engines/updates/nsf-publishes-data-letters-intent-submitted-rie) (July 2024)
- [The 71 teams invited to submit full proposals, with their coalitions](https://www.nsf.gov/tip/updates/explore-data-collaborate-71-nsf-regional-innovation-engines) (November 2024; [interactive map and data](https://tableau.external.nsf.gov/views/NSFEnginesFullProposalInvitations/MapOverview))
- [29 semifinalists](https://www.nsf.gov/tip/updates/nsf-advances-29-semifinalists-second-nsf-regional-innovation) (July 2025)
- [15 finalists](https://www.nsf.gov/news/nsf-selects-15-finalists-advance-next-round-its-second) (September 2025)
- [NSF Engines Development Awards](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/regional-innovation-engines/portfolio/nsf-engines-development-awards) (planning grants, 2023-2024)

## What we collected

- **One table of all teams**: each team from its letter of intent to the furthest stage it reached, with its
  lead organisation, states, principal investigator and keywords at each stage.
- **The members of each coalition**, at the invited stage (all `r nrow(props)` teams) and in the full proposal
  (the 29 semifinalists).
- Stages are linked by lead organisation or, where it changed, by the proposal title; one link was decided by
  hand. The investigators' email addresses are not kept.

## First findings

**Who leads the teams.** Universities led most letters of intent and almost every team that reached the end;
teams led by companies rarely went past the letter of intent.

```{r leaders}
furthest <- lois |> left_join(props |> select(team_id, stage), by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(stage = coalesce(stage, "loi"), type = str_remove(lead_org_type, " \\(.*\\)$"))
at <- function(s) furthest$stage %in% s
tab <- furthest |>
  mutate(invited = at(c("preliminary", "semifinalist", "finalist", "engine")),
         semi = at(c("semifinalist", "finalist", "engine")), final = at(c("finalist", "engine")), eng = at("engine")) |>
  group_by(`Lead organisation (from the letter of intent)` = type) |>
  summarise(`Letters of intent` = n(), Invited = sum(invited), Semifinalists = sum(semi),
            Finalists = sum(final), `NSF Engines` = sum(eng), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(`Letters of intent`))
kable(tab, format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed"')
```

**How much the winners changed.** For the `r nrow(chg)` Engines, the core of the bid stayed from the letter of
intent to the award, while the people at the head and especially the coalition changed:

- the lead organisation is the same at every stage for `r sum(chg$lead_org_same)` of `r nrow(chg)` Engines;
- the states are the same in the letter of intent and the invited proposal for `r sum(chg$states_same)`;
- the principal investigator is the same person at every stage, including the award today, for only
  `r sum(chg$pi_same)`; some changed between proposals, some after the award;
- the coalition grew from a median of `r round(median(chg$coalition_preliminary))` members at the invited stage to
  `r round(median(chg$coalition_full))` in the full proposal, and about `r round(100 * median(chg$coalition_kept))`% of the
  earlier members are still named (a lower bound: names are compared as written).

So comparisons of winners and other teams should use the coalitions of one stage: the invited stage for all
`r nrow(props)` teams, the full proposal for the 29 semifinalists.
